title: Adaptive guardian orchestration and staged dry-run fallback
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Summary:
Design and implement an "adaptive guardian" subsystem that provides per-dependency / per-model / per-tenant safety controls (trip rules, staged thresholds, and orchestration for safe fallback). The goal is to reduce blast radius during spikes or degraded dependencies while preserving end-user latency SLOs and maintaining clear observability for rollouts.

Motivation:
- Current per-tenant/model fallbacks are ad-hoc and cause sudden, opaque degradations when thresholds are crossed.
- We need a unified control plane that can: 1) evaluate multi-signal trip decisions (latency P95, error-rate, saturating queues), 2) run non-invasive dry-run simulations, 3) execute staged fallback choreography (lenient -> restricted -> queued) and 4) provide a canary + rollout path for new thresholds.

Proposal (high level):
1) Rule engine: deterministic, ordered rulebook per tenant+model+dependency. A rule can be a set of AND/OR predicates over signals (P95 latency, 95th queue length, error-rate, downstream 5xx ratio, region availability). Rules evaluate to actions with priority and cooldown windows.
2) Modes: "monitor-only" (dry-run), "adaptive" (automated staged enforcement), and "manual" (PM/ops triggered). Dry-run collects proposed actions into telemetry without affecting traffic.
3) Staged actions:
   - stage-0: soft-shed prefixes (prefer cached responses, shorten max tokens)
   - stage-1: probabilistic degradation (X% of requests routed to lower-cost/compatible model variant)
   - stage-2: strict shedding (reject with standardized 503+hint or queue with tokenized backoff)
   - stage-3: tenant-level throttle / failover to alternate region or dedicated cap
4) Fallback choreography: specify fallback graph mapping model variants, regions, or synthetic responses. Actions include metadata for user-facing hints and rollout rollbacks.

SLO & metrics mapping:
- Primary SLOs: 99.9% model request success (2xx) within 400ms P95 for low-latency tier; fallbacks must preserve SLO at system level.
- Trip thresholds (examples):
   - latency-based: P95 > 420ms for 2m window AND 10% of servers above CPU 85% => stage-1 dry-run, stage-2 enforce after 5m sustained
   - error-based: 5xx rate > 1% over 1m => immediate stage-1 enforcement for affected routes
   - queue saturation: avg queue > 150ms AND queue length > 500 => prefunnel to cached responses
- Observability hooks: every rule evaluation emits event with evaluated signals, decision path, action id, and correlation id. Aggregate events used for alerting and SLO dashboards.

Telemetry & safety checks:
- Dry-run mode must be default for all new rules. Provide an "impact estimator" dashboard predicting %requests moved at each stage and estimated SLO delta.
- Safety guard: every enforced stage increments a progressive enforcement counter; automated rollback triggers if error-rate or user-visible error budget burn exceeds configured threshold within 10m.

API & config: 
- New resource: GuardianRule (namespaced by tenant, model, region) with fields: name, predicates (list), action (enum), priority, cooldown_secs, mode (monitor|adaptive|manual), dry_run_end (timestamp).
- Admin endpoints for dry-run activation, force-enforce, rollback, and simulation.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): implement rule engine + dry-run only; UI to create rules and view impact estimates.
- Phase 2 (2 weeks): implement staged enforcement actions and enforcement counters; limited canary to internal beta tenants + infra team.
- Phase 3 (2 weeks): widen to top-5 tenants with SLAs, add multi-region failover integration.
- Phase 4: production roll (release runtime-1.21) with opt-in via console and default conservative thresholds.

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests for rule evaluation logic with boundary cases.
- Integration test harness that replays realistic telemetry (derived from last quarter traces) and asserts decisions align with expected stage.
- Chaos testing: induce region-level latency and verify fallback choreography and rollback behavior.

Runbooks & ops:
- Runbook for ops: how to inspect rule evaluations, how to pause/disable a rule, how to escalate during cascading fallbacks.
- Alerting: new alert when enforcement count for a tenant increases by >10x in 15m or when rollback was auto-triggered.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: over-eager shedding could reduce quality for high-value tenants. Mitigation: conservative defaults, per-tenant opt-outs, and dry-run must precede enforcement.
- Risk: rule complexity causing nondeterministic decisions. Mitigation: deterministic ordering, bounded evaluation time and reject rules that exceed compile budget.
